Thanks for the usage file — that makes this much easier. High level options we can offer (summaries below; I'll attach a formal quote and SLA addendum):

• Option A — Premium SLA (P95 200ms), 12-month term, 4 dedicated burst slots, 24/7 on-call, 8h incident response for Sev1: +18% price uplift on current ARR.
• Option B — Pilot premium SLA (3-month trial), 2 burst slots, P95 target with staircase band (start 250ms -> 200ms after tuning): +10% uplift, then re-price at renewal.

Forwarding BlueWave's ask (see Laura's note + usage file). Proposal I'm leaning to:

- Push for Option A (committed premium SLA) but soften commercially: 12-month term, 18% uplift, include 2 months of on-call credits (applied to first invoice) and a 60-day performance tuning window where we agree a staircase SLO (250ms -> 200ms).

Chloe —

Looks good. A few suggested edits before we send to BlueWave:

1) Latency: put a "staircased latency band" into the SLA: P95 target 250ms for first 60 days, then 200ms subject to three acceptance prompt sets. If acceptance fails, we automatically fall back to the standard model variant but maintain the 24/7 support credit.
2) Capacity: define "burst slot" as a reserve token bucket (4 slots = N concurrent generator workers). Include soft-cap language and explicit overage rate ($0.XX per token over agreed bursted volume).
3) Credits: limit on-call credit to incident-reported hours (max 120 hours credit over first 2 months) to avoid open-ended credits.
4) Commercial: drop to 17% uplift if they sign a 24-month committed term; stay at 18% for 12-month term with credits. Gives us a path to extend.

I'll mark up the SLA_Addendum_BlueWave_v2.pdf and send a redline. If you're comfortable with the 17/18% cadence, we can present both options and let Laura take it to procurement.

Ben
